title: Expand globs safely with compgen, and scope IFS for any structured parse
summary: Do not let a pattern you mean to match explode as an unquoted argument, and do not split structured lines on the default IFS when the fields themselves can hold spaces. Expand into a variable via a bounded tool, and set IFS to the one delimiter you mean for the one read it trims, keeping the change local.
technique: Compgen expands a glob into candidate matches that you then filter; a `while IFS= read -r m; do` loop with a local IFS safely splits CSV/tab text field by field; arrays written to a sourced file are re-read safely by sourcing and checking `declare -p` rather than text-slicing.
evidence_note: queuebash.sh:96-104 expands with compgen -G and filters `[[ -d "$m" ]]`. assets.d/queue.sh:73 sets `local IFS=','` for a CSV scan, line 149 uses `IFS=$'\t' read -r qid state name ts cmd`, and lines 84-93 source a job file then gate on `declare -p COMMAND`.
invariants: Never let an unquoted glob expand directly in an argument position you only meant to test.
Scope IFS to the exact delimiter for the exact read/scan that needs splitting, via `local IFS=...` or a subshell.
Prefer structured re-reads (source + declare -p presence) over slicing persisted collections.
A split loop must treat an empty entry as still an entry, never accidentally skip it.
